**Visual observations from test image:**
- Close-up of a soybean stem at a node
- Gray-white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth concentrated at the node junction
- Surrounding leaves are yellowing (plant stress/dying)
- Stem otherwise appears green/intact

**Analysis:**
The fluffy gray-white mycelial mass at the stem node is the hallmark sign of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). The reference images confirm this pattern — cottony white mycelium growing on stems at nodes, with surrounding tissue collapse. The yellowing leaves indicate systemic plant decline from the stem infection. No other class produces this characteristic cottony fungal growth at nodes; Charcoal Rot would show gray discoloration with dark microsclerotia (not fluffy), and other stem diseases show lesions without visible mycelium.
